source.title: Less LLM, More Documents: Searching for Improved RAG
source.authors: Jing-Jie Ning; Yi-Bo Kong; Yunfan Long; James P. Callan

record.tranche_reason: Evaluates downstream QA scores across Qwen3 parameter scales in a RAG setting, bearing on downstream scaling (V6), but does not measure held-out pretraining loss or fit power laws.
record.gate_note: The paper reports RAG QA results while varying corpus size and generator size. Only the endpoint corpus scales (1 and 12 shards) are extracted below for each model, dataset, and metric. The paper also reports gold-answer coverage, context-benefited success, utilization ratios, catch-up thresholds, serving-compute estimates, and paired bootstrap comparisons; these do not test the claim versions about pretraining loss or compute-optimal training allocation.
record.test_reason: The study varies Qwen3 generator size (0.6B–14B) in a RAG QA setting, so its results bear weakly on V6: whether downstream task scores rise with model scale. The size comparison is a by-product of a corpus–generator trade-off study. It fits no scaling law and tests no loss link. T3 (new setting) fits better than T2, since the paper does not aim at the V6 question.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Authors conclude that corpus scaling reliably improves RAG QA and can often offset one to two generator-size tiers, with diminishing returns beyond about 5x corpus. Gains come from higher gold-answer coverage while utilization stays stable. Mid-sized generators benefit most; tiny and very large models benefit less. They do not claim anything about scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: This is a RAG evaluation varying generator parameter tier and retrieval-corpus shards, not a pretraining loss sweep, power-law fit, or compute-optimal training experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: QA scores and corpus-compensation thresholds vary with dataset, model size, corpus scale, and forward versus reversed shard ordering. The authors note that Qwen3 sizes may have minor training-recipe differences.

fits_no_version.finding: Enlarging the retrieval corpus (1→12 shards of ClueWeb22-A) raises RAG QA with diminishing returns. Paired-bootstrap CIs include zero from about 4–5 shards on, and the smaller model needs more corpus to match the next tier.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In modular RAG with a fixed evidence budget, retrieval-corpus scale improves QA with diminishing returns and can partially substitute for generator size.

fits_no_version.finding: Context utilization ratio is not monotonic in model size: 1.7B and 4B peak near 42%, while 14B lags (Fig. 9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ability to use retrieved context does not grow monotonically with generator size.

record.problems: Results are limited to open-domain QA using a 30% subset of ClueWeb22-A and Qwen3 models; the authors note possible pretraining-data overlap, residual shard-quality gradients, and minor recipe differences across model sizes. The table scores extracted here do not report uncertainty; paired-bootstrap uncertainty is discussed for adjacent-shard F1 differences in the text/figure.
record.rows_left_out: The intermediate shard-count results from Tables 1, 3, and 4 are omitted to stay within 60 rows; also omitted are separate measurements in Figures 3–11 and the Appendix concerning reversed shard order, gold-answer coverage, CB rates, utilization ratios, and paired bootstrap differences. They are outside the tested claim versions or are not tabulated as exact values in the text.

untested.parts: No shape comparisons at fixed size.
No other modality or training regime. Retrieval-corpus scaling is inference-time and has no power-law fit.
Predictability (any fitted functional form), link to pretraining loss, sizes beyond 14B. Qwen3 sizes may differ in training recipe, so this is not a controlled scale sweep.
No exponents or fitting choices compared.

missing.what: Closed-book (no-retrieval) Known Rate by model size, the most direct downstream-vs-size measure free of retrieval effects
Utilization Ratio by model size, non-monotonic in size

record.verdict_notes: The study's evidence on V6 is incidental: five Qwen3 sizes with possibly different recipes, no fit and no predictability test. The reader's claim that both metrics increase at every tier is false on WebQ (WQ-1-14-EM). Per-row 'observed' states are not meaningful without a baseline; each row's baseline should be the next-smaller model's score.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining cross-entropy scaling with parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Predicting much larger runs from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with training compute.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes.
No relationship to pretraining loss or explicit predictive fit is tested; evaluation is limited to RAG open-domain QA on three benchmarks and Qwen3 models.
No fitting choices or exponents for pretraining loss scaling laws or compute-optimal allocation are compared.

relationships.condition: Qwen3 0.6B–14B RAG QA on NQ and TriviaQA, 1 and 12 shards
relationships.reason: F1 and EM rise monotonically with generator size at every tier. Examples: NQ-1 F1 25.37→44.26 (NQ-1-06-F1..NQ-1-14-F1) and TQA-12 F1 57.86→82.00. No predictive fit is tested.
relationships.display_finding: F1 and exact match increased at every generator size, including NQ F1 from 25.37 to 44.26 with one shard and TriviaQA F1 from 57.86 to 82.00 with twelve shards.

relationships.reason: Gains flatten above 4B. At 1 shard, 14B EM 21.65 falls below 8B 21.70 and F1 rises only 0.36 (WQ-1-14-EM, WQ-1-14-F1). At 12 shards, F1 rises only 39.41→40.69 from 4B to 14B.
relationships.display_finding: With one shard, 14B exact match was 21.65 versus 8B's 21.70, while F1 gained only 0.36 points; with 12 shards, scaling from 4B to 14B raised F1 only from 39.41 to 40.69.

relationships.reason: F1 rises clearly from 0.6B to 4B (27.63→37.01 at 1 shard; 32.00→39.41 at 12 shards).
relationships.display_finding: F1 increased from 27.63 to 37.01 with one shard and from 32.00 to 39.41 with twelve shards.

reader_labels.condition: Qwen3-0.6B through Qwen3-14B on NQ, TriviaQA, and WebQ at corpus scales of 1 and 12 shards
reader_labels.reason: At each matched dataset and corpus scale, both reported QA metrics increase with generator size across the listed model tiers (rows NQ-1-06-F1 through WQ-12-14-EM).
